_note: Copy rules for every social graphic and its caption (2026-10-21; 2026-10-22 Phase 1: editorialBrief, pieceRubric, claims, style, week; content/copy_check.py, the german-editorial skill, brief.template.json _help.copyRules). The examples: brand/copy_examples.json (the approved brand references, verbatim). Checked for free before every dry run of a paid build (copy check), then shown to the user in the copy review (`ca content copy`, `ca calendar copy`); images are made only for approved copy. A failing item is rewritten once, then it stops (never sent to image generation). ctas: the button labels, each mapped to the verified service ids of config/services.json it fits ("any": every service; insightOnly: also for an insight-only post); the CTA icon follows its meaning (workflows/design_render.cta_icon: the calendar only for booking, else the circle arrow).
audience: Inhaber, Geschäftsführer und Führungskräfte kleiner und mittlerer Unternehmen in Deutschland (Mittelstand): keine Techniker. Sie wollen wissen, was ein Thema für ihr Unternehmen bedeutet und was es ihnen bringt (Zeit, Kosten, Kunden, Wachstum, Sicherheit).

angles.news: a news or society topic: what does this mean for the reader's business (or life), and what should they do now?
angles.service: a service topic: what pain does this remove for the reader, and what do they gain?

rubric.readerCentred: speaks to the reader (Sie/Ihr, du/dein) or about their business, not about technology
rubric.concreteBenefit: names a gain the reader wants (time, customers, costs, growth, calm), not a task
rubric.emotionalHook: a contrast, a benefit pair, a question to the reader or a bold future statement
rubric.fitsVisual: the visual concept can show it in one concrete scene

editorialBrief._note: Phase 1 P1-R1 (2026-10-22): copyPlan.editorial, written before any copy (german-editorial skill, references/editorial-brief.md). proof.source: a cited article ID (sourceArticleIds or an insight's source), a link listed in research.md, proof.md (brand/proof.md) or service:<verified service id>.

pieceRubric._note: P1-R6: copyPlan.review.scores, Codex's self-review of the whole piece (graphic and caption), 0 (missing), 1 (partly) or 2 (clearly) per criterion. Below minTotal, a criterion below minEach or a mustBeFull criterion below 2: one rewrite, then the copy review shows it STOPPED (never dropped).

criteria.singleIdea: one clear idea the reader can repeat in one sentence (the editorial coreIdea)
criteria.relevance: matters to the German business reader of the brief: time, money, customers, risk or calm
criteria.specificity: one real number, case or opinion from the proof; no line that fits any topic
criteria.naturalGerman: reads like a German business writer: active verbs, short sentences, no Nominalstil, no anglicism where a common German word exists
criteria.hook: the first words make the reader stop: a contrast, a benefit pair, a question or a bold statement (copy_examples.json patterns)
criteria.truth: every fact, number, name and promise is covered by the editorial proof, the insights or the verified services; no invented case, client or result
criteria.ctaFit: the action fits the piece and the service: action verb plus what the reader gets (the category's ctas)
criteria.platformFit: follows the category's platform rules (german-editorial references/platforms.md) and differs from the same topic on other platforms

claims._note: P1-R5: free, deterministic. In the graphic copy, the caption and the ad texts: numbers (a scenario timing before a scenarioUnits word, 24/7 and a count before an ownCounts word excepted), percentages, euro amounts, years, organisation names (organisations, or a name with an inner capital such as OpenAI) and studyWords statements must be found in the evidence: the editorial proof, the insights, research.md and the cited articles, brand/proof.md and the verified services (config/services.json). Otherwise the item fails with "unbelegte Aussage". allowNames are never claims (channels, the brand).
claims._numberWordsNote: 2026-10-22: written numbers from zwei upwards are claims like digits ("vier Tools", "sieben von zehn"); ein/eine never are. The evidence may hold the digits, the German word or the English word (englishNumberWords). shareWords: a share of a group is a claim too; one of its markers must be in the evidence.

style._note: P1-R2/R7 warnings in the copy review (never blocking): a caption or ad-text sentence over sentenceMaxWords words; a sentence with nounChainMin or more nouns ending in nounSuffixes (Nominalstil: write the verb).

week._note: P1-R3/R4 warnings of the week's copy review: a headline pattern chosen by more than maxSamePattern rows; headlines or captions of the same topic (the same research source) on different platforms at or above similarity (content/topic_pool.similarity, 0-1).

facebook_ad.goal: an offer with a strong CTA: the pain, the offer, the next step

facebook_post.goal: an insight with a business takeaway for the reader and a soft CTA

linkedin_post.goal: an insight with a business takeaway for decision makers and a soft CTA

instagram_carousel.goal: a trend or provocation hook on the cover, one idea per slide, the last slide asks for engagement

bodyMaxWordsBySlide._note: 2026-10-22: the slide type's layout limit (design_directions.json point body hint: at most 35 words) is the hard limit of the middle slides; bodyMaxWords is for the cover and the last slide only

roman._note: Roman's founder variants (FB-R1, FA-R1, LI-R1): the same headline and body quality as the category, plus 3 benefit chips (the features zone) and a full body line under the headline, never a thin one-liner.
